title: Recent vLLM versions report no available memory for cache blocks on models that fit with vLLM 0.2.4
body: Since vLLM 0.2.5, I can no longer run a Llama 2 70B 4-bit AWQ model on 4 A10G GPUs even though it worked with older vLLM versions; I hit this with docker images built on cuda 11.8 with vllm 0.2.5 or 0.2.6. I also see similar problems when starting two 7B models on one 80GB A100. For example, two instances can start when the first uses gpu_memory_utilization=0.4 and the second uses 0.6, but setting the second to 0.4 raises "No available memory for the cache blocks. Try increasing gpu_memory_utilization" despite GPU memory still being available.

symptoms_visible: Since vLLM 0.2.5, my Llama 2 70B 4-bit AWQ deployment no longer starts on four A10G GPUs even though it worked with older vLLM.
When I start two 7B servers on one A100, the second raises 'No available memory for the cache blocks' at gpu_memory_utilization=0.4 but starts at 0.6.
N0.label: N0 cache-block regression reported

symptoms_visible: A single sharded 70B AWQ model fails to start with vLLM 0.2.5 or later on four otherwise-empty A10G GPUs.
The same model and GPUs run normally with vLLM 0.2.4 and leave enough room for sustained use.
N1.label: N1 dedicated-GPU regression confirmed

symptoms_visible: The large tensor-parallel model still reaches zero available GPU cache blocks during startup.
N2.label: N2 profiling measurements collected

symptoms_visible: With PR 2031 temporarily reverted, the server gets past the cache-block check, but the same long-context query ends in a GPU out-of-memory error.
N3_x.label: N3_x profiling-revert aftermath

symptoms_visible: The 70B AWQ model starts and runs on my four A10G GPUs when I add --enforce-eager.
For two 7B servers sharing one GPU, I can start them sequentially by using 0.4 for the first and about 0.9 for the second after the first has fully loaded.
N4.label: N4 eager mode and shared-GPU behavior verified

symptoms_visible: --enforce-eager works to solve this issue for my 4*A10G 70B AWQ deployment.
Both 7B services can run on the shared GPU when they are started sequentially with the later instance's utilization value accounting for memory already occupied.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Are the four A10G GPUs empty and dedicated to this vLLM instance, or are other GPU processes running?
Does the 70B failure occur on clean GPUs or only when the GPUs are shared?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The four A10G GPUs are clean. Nothing else is using them.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The GPUs are shared with several other models that already occupy most of their memory.
The GPUs are dedicated, apart from a few megabytes used by normal driver state.

question_patterns: Is the main failure the two-model shared-GPU case, or does one tensor-parallel 70B model also fail by itself?
Can you isolate the issue to a single sharded model on the four GPUs?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The primary issue is one 70B AWQ model sharded across the four A10Gs. Forget the two-model case for now: that single model no longer fits on 0.2.5 or later.

question_patterns: Does the identical model and workload run on vLLM 0.2.4?
Was 0.2.4 only able to start, or could it also handle the long-context workload reliably?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: vLLM 0.2.4 and lower work perfectly on the same four A10Gs, leave plenty of room, and have handled heavy use for long periods.

edges.comment: The reporter repeatedly clarified that the primary regression was a single 70B AWQ model on four clean A10Gs, not merely contention between two models.

question_patterns: Can you log torch.cuda.mem_get_info before and after model_runner.profile_run and paste the raw values?
What free-memory values do you observe immediately before and after the profiling forward pass?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On my 70B BF16 test across eight A100 40GB GPUs, I see about 22GB free per GPU before model_runner.profile_run(), then only about 0.26GB free per GPU after it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Free memory remains around 22GB before and after profile_run(), even though vLLM still reports zero cache blocks.
The values are about 21.5GB before profile_run() and 0.4GB afterward on an otherwise equivalent tensor-parallel run.

edges.comment: The profiling measurements and decoder-layer logs came from another affected contributor and are folded into the simulated user side. The answer contains raw observed memory values only; interpreting fragmentation and cache estimation is engineer-side.

solution.intent: Revert PR 2031 and restore the pre-0.2.5 torch-only peak-memory calculation so startup allocates cache blocks as it did in vLLM 0.2.4.
solution.concrete_example: Temporarily revert PR 2031 in worker.py and use torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() for peak_memory instead of deriving the peak from total minus free GPU memory.

edges.comment: The reporter tested the proposed revert in a temporary source checkout. It bypassed the title error but caused a real GPU OOM on the same long-context query, so reverting the accounting change is not the resolution.

question_patterns: Can you restore the normal vLLM code, add --enforce-eager, and rerun the 70B AWQ workload on the four A10Gs?
Please disable CUDA graph execution with --enforce-eager and report whether the same model starts and handles the workload.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Adding --enforce-eager works for my four-A10G 70B AWQ setup. The model starts and runs instead of failing with the cache-block error.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same cache-block error occurs with --enforce-eager, with zero GPU blocks reported.
It works with --enforce-eager, but startup is a little slower than before.

edges.comment: This is a handler-initiated configuration probe and therefore a clarification-only measurement, even though --enforce-eager is also the working deployment setting. The reporter later volunteered the separate sequential-startup behavior for two models sharing one GPU.

solution.intent: Keep the corrected memory accounting and drop the extra CUDA graph capture footprint that vLLM enables by default from 0.2.6 onward, by running the four-A10G deployment with --enforce-eager; treat shared-GPU instances separately by starting them sequentially and making each later gpu_memory_utilization value cumulative with memory already occupied.
solution.concrete_example: For the 70B AWQ server, restore the unmodified vLLM code and launch with --enforce-eager, then verify the same long-context request. If two 7B instances must share one GPU, wait for the first to finish loading; for example, start it at 0.4 and start the second at about 0.9 so the later calculation includes memory already occupied by the first.
solution.inference_hint: The user supplied raw memory readings, the version boundary, and the outcomes of the revert and --enforce-eager tests. Engineers connected those observations to PR 2031's total-minus-free accounting, which shipped in 0.2.5 and is the mechanism for the earliest failing version, together with tensor-parallel/profile-run fragmentation or reserved allocations. CUDA graph capture is a separate, additional startup consumer that only exists and is enabled by default from 0.2.6 onward, so it explains extra pressure on the versions the reporter is running now, not the original 0.2.5 break; disabling it with --enforce-eager frees enough headroom for the four-A10G deployment. For shared GPUs, the current calculation includes memory already occupied when a later instance profiles itself, which explains why its utilization value must include the earlier instance rather than represent only its own intended fraction.

edges.comment: The reporter's resolution was --enforce-eager for the clean four-A10G 70B AWQ deployment. The two-model scenario was resolved separately by sequential startup and cumulative utilization values. Release scheduling and later unrelated hardware reports are omitted.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the clean multi-GPU failure as a startup cache-profiling/memory-accounting regression that begins in vLLM 0.2.5: the newer total-minus-free accounting charges tensor-parallel/profile-run fragmentation and non-torch allocations against the budget, so the four-A10G 70B AWQ case is left with zero cache blocks. The extra CUDA graph capture footprint is an additional consumer only from vLLM 0.2.6 onward, where graph capture is on by default; it must not be offered as the mechanism for the original 0.2.5 break.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the version comparison, clean dedicated GPUs, the raw free-memory drop around profile_run, and the successful --enforce-eager test.
Must recommend --enforce-eager for the reporter's four-A10G 70B AWQ deployment and verify both startup and the representative long-context workload.

Must not recommend reverting PR 2031 or restoring the old torch-only peak-memory calculation as the final fix, because that bypassed the cache-block error but produced GPU OOM on the same long-context query.

Must distinguish the shared-GPU case: start instances sequentially and set a later instance's gpu_memory_utilization cumulatively to account for memory already occupied, rather than assigning both instances the same independent fraction.
Must treat the issue as resolved only after the reporter verifies the deployment behavior.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical ML infrastructure user who builds CUDA containers, serves quantized tensor-parallel models, compares vLLM versions, modifies source code for tests, and can validate behavior across A10G, A100, and H100 systems.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and evidence-driven; supplies complete commands and traces, repeatedly narrows discussion back to the primary reproduction, and reports workaround results concisely.
